## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}

A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check |

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

# Testing and verification

## Use the preconfigured Linux CLI

Run `scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh` on an Ubuntu worker to install the pinned
CLI, Chromium, Mesa Vulkan drivers, and a persistent Xvfb display. Let the reusable
workflow run this before publishing SSH access. Use `playwright-cli` from Actions
or a fresh SSH shell; let the wrapper supply DISPLAY and the Linux configuration.
Use `playwright-cli -s=check open <url>`, `eval`, `screenshot`, and `close` without
manual browser flags. Load `.github/templates/linux.md` by default. Select `mac.md` instead when
a `mac` label or `#mac` hashtag is present. Match case insensitively. Recheck the actual screenshot after upgrades.

## Capture the Linux WebGPU triangle

Install Playwright 1.63.0 and its full Chromium browser as below. Install
`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve
`tests/fixtures/webgpu-triangle.html` over localhost HTTP. Run:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-runtime xvfb-run -a node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/webgpu-triangle.html --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --backend swiftshader --require-green-triangle --out /tmp/linux-triangle
```

Require green triangle pixels, a usable device, `scene.webgpu.rendered=true`,
and no page errors. Inspect the image. Treat SwiftShader and Mesa llvmpipe as
CPU rendering, not GPU hardware acceleration. Use the headed Xvfb result on
[run 34908797646](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/actions/runs/34908797646)
as the verified 2026-09-15 reference. Do not accept the headless result from
that run: its initial generic pixel check falsely accepted background pixels.
Retain the fixture's GPU reference. Preserve failed diagnostics when investigating
`A valid external Instance reference no longer exists`. Do not infer a single
root cause from the combined driver-installation and fixture changes.
Use `--backend vulkan` for native-driver experiments, `--backend swangle` for
ANGLE SwiftShader experiments, and `--executable` to select another browser.
Keep the default Metal path for the Mac test.

## Capture Pascal Editor on Linux

Use `http://localhost:3002`, not the numeric loopback origin, with the default
Pascal Next.js development server. Check the server log for blocked development
resources when HTTP 403 or HMR handshake errors occur.
Install dependencies with the repository's Bun lockfile. Start `bun dev` and
wait for the editor on port 3002. Create a studio through `POST /api/scenes`
using the documented scene structure. Open `/scene/<id>?disable=postFx` for
the reduced-effects capture. Do not use the empty root page as a scene test.
Run headed Chromium under Xvfb with the tested SwiftShader flags above.
Wait for visible geometry; verify the existing canvas accepts `webgpu` and
rejects `webgl2`. Require the viewer's `WebGPU device ready` log, no failed
HTTP requests, and no JavaScript errors. Inspect the screenshot manually.
Treat the 2026-09-15 room capture on issue 113 as a software-rendering result.
Do not claim full post-processing coverage. Preserve readiness-timeout warnings
in the report; do not confuse an earlier WebGL fallback capture with the final
WebGPU capture. Keep the saved scene and application server for further tests.

## Capture WebGPU on a hosted Mac

Use full Chromium with the Metal backend. Keep Playwright's other launch defaults. Test
headed mode first; use `--headless` only after comparing the actual captures.
Install Playwright and its full Chromium build in a separate runtime directory:

```sh
npm install --prefix /tmp/gpu-capture-runtime playwright@1.63.0
/tmp/gpu-capture-runtime/node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium
PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT=/tmp/gpu-capture-runtime node scripts/gpu-capture.mjs \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/ --canvas '#wgpu' \
  --require-metal --out /tmp/game-capture
```

Replace the URL and canvas selector with the running game's values. Start the
game before capture if it requires user input. Read `diagnostic.json`,
`canvas.png`, and `page.png` from the output directory. Require an available
WebGPU device, no page errors, and painted canvas pixels. Exclude CSS borders
from the pixel check. Accept a flat triangle with two interior colours; reject
a uniform interior even when its border has another colour.

Use `--baseline` to test full Chromium without extra flags. Use `--headless`
to test the same full browser headlessly. Do not substitute the separate
headless shell. Preserve failed diagnostics; do not silently skip absent
adapters. Keep Vulkan flags out of the macOS Metal capture path.

Use the verified flags: `--enable-gpu`, `--ignore-gpu-blocklist`,
`--enable-unsafe-webgpu`, and `--use-angle=metal`. Check `chrome://gpu` in a
separate headed page. Interpret `Apple Paravirtual device` as a virtual Metal
adapter, not proof of a physical GPU model or hardware performance.

Refer to [Playwright's browser documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers#opt-in-to-new-headless-mode)
for the full-browser/headless-shell distinction. Reproduce the evidence from
[issue #110](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/issues/110) and
[run 34801504801](https://github.com/AgentsLoop/PlayGround/actions/runs/34801504801).
Use the 2026-09-14 result as a reference, not a promise for later runner images:
Playwright 1.63.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12 acquired vendor `apple`,
`isFallbackAdapter=false`, and a usable WebGPU device. Both headed and headless
Metal captures visibly showed the green triangle; pure headed baseline also
succeeded. Run `node --test scripts/gpu-capture.test.mjs` for the pixel and
symlink-entry regressions, then repeat the live screenshot test.

## Test standalone issue access

Create an issue with the `OpenCode` label and `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone`.
Verify that Actions starts one execution job.
Restore the access variable after testing. Verify restricted access with the
variable unset. Verify one Actions run for each new issue.

## Test the `-rc` repository at a selected commit

Use the release-candidate repository when you need to test the workflow against
an older or experimental commit without changing the source repository.

Set the repository and commit variables first:

```sh
repo=denaidark/OhMyGithub-rc
commit=<full-commit-sha>
branch=rc-<short-commit-sha>
```

Create a branch from the exact commit and make it the GitHub default branch:

```sh
git push "https://github.com/$repo.git" "${commit}:refs/heads/$branch"
gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch "$branch"
gh repo view "$repo" --json defaultBranchRef
```

Keep the existing `main` branch and older test branches. Use a new branch name
for each commit so the tested revision remains clear and recoverable. The
workflow checks out the GitHub default branch when the issue title has no
branch metadata.

Create an SSH test issue with the required labels:

```sh
gh issue create --repo "$repo" \
  --title "Check SSH connectivity on $branch" \
  --body $'# Check SSH connectivity on <branch>\n\nVerify the temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, authentication, tunnel, and remote response. Record concrete evidence without exposing secrets.' \
  --label Goal --label ssh --label OpenCode
```

Create the issue after listener installation to trigger one native `issues` run. The
`Goal` label selects goal mode. The `ssh` label requests an SSH-only check in
the reusable workflow. Verify the issue labels and the selected checkout:

```sh
gh issue view <issue-number> --repo "$repo" --json labels
gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow opencode.yml --limit 5 \
  --json databaseId,displayTitle,event,status,url,headBranch
```

Confirm `event` is `issues` and `headBranch` is the default branch.
Check preparation outputs for the selected `target_ref` and `target_sha`.

Discover and follow the temporary SSH connection with the repository helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo "$repo"
```

Run the helper while the Actions job is active. It reports no command after the
worker closes the tunnel. If it reports no command at the start, inspect the
run steps and logs before changing the SSH secret. `AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED:
true` proves that GitHub received the public-key secret; it does not prove that
the tunnel or SSH service started.

After testing, restore the normal default branch if required:

```sh
gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch main
```

Project acceptance testing is live production testing. Manually create a real
GitHub issue with the required labels and prompt, then verify the resulting
issue run, exactly one execution runner/session, and the completed production
outcome. Do not use unit tests as the testing strategy; local checks such as
`actionlint` and `git diff --check` are only static safeguards before the live
test.

For an issue-triggered run with `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` configured, verify
these checkpoints in order:

1. `Start AgentsWeb SSH session` succeeds.
2. `Post temporary SSH connection command` succeeds.
3. `Verify AgentsWeb SSH availability` succeeds.
4. `Run OpenCode` succeeds.
5. `Mark SSH session closed` and `Clean up AgentsWeb SSH session` succeed.
6. The expected branch and immutable commit exist.

The verification loop must confirm a browser entrypoint before public-app and
Pages checks: either `$PROJECT_DIR/index.html` or `$PROJECT_DIR/dist/index.html`
must exist, and remediation retries must repeat that check. Static root
`index.html` apps are copied to a temporary Pages directory; built
`dist/index.html` apps are published directly.

When `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` is missing, the SSH session and SSH-based
verification steps must be skipped. OpenCode Web, the Cloudflare session URL,
and the browser-based workflow path must still run; the access comment should
omit SSH instructions and cleanup must not report an SSH session closure.

The AgentsWeb public port must be derived from `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, not
`GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`. Run numbers restart at `1` for each repository, which made

```js
function buildTile({seed, dark, windowColors, minW=70,maxW=160,minH=220,maxH=520, width=2048, height=620}) {
 const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width=width; c.height=height;
 const g = c.getContext('2d');
 const rng = makeRng(seed);
 let x=0;
 while (x < width) {
   const w=rand...; const h=...; 
   const y=height-h;
   // building body
   g.fillStyle = dark; g.fillRect(x,y,w,h);
   // edge highlight
   g.fillStyle='rgba(...)'; g.fillRect(x,y,1,h)
   // roof details
   ...
   // windows
   const cols=Math.floor(w/18), rows=Math.floor(h/22);
   for (...) if (rng()<windowChance) { color; g.fillRect(...) }
   x += w + rand(2,16);
 }
 return c;
}
```

## Objective
- Build a polished stickman beat 'em up ("smash 'em up") browser game, as requested in Spanish: "Quiero un juego de stickman, quiero se se pueda pelear en ese juego como un smash it up".

## Requirements
- Stickman characters with beat 'em up combat (combos, enemies, boss).
- Browser-playable, no external assets/frameworks; static project served on port 3002.
- Must support desktop and mobile touch controls per repository mobile-game conventions.
- Verify in a real browser with screenshots, not just unit tests.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS ES modules + Canvas 2D; no package.json/Vite (project is detected as static `index.html` by default runtime).
- Spanish UI.
- Neon-noir rainy city rooftop/street theme; procedural stick figures and WebAudio-synthesized SFX/music.
- Single continuous stage, 5 waves including final boss "EL REY".
- Controls: WASD/arrows move, J/Z punch (3-hit combo), K/X kick, Space jump, Shift/B block, Q/Ctrl dodge, L/C special (50 fury), Esc/P pause, M mute, Enter start.
- Start button text "JUGAR" with `aria-label="Play game"` so the capture harness auto-clicks it.
- Static background layers baked to offscreen canvases (sky, ground strip, sign sprites) for performance; world renderer was just rewritten accordingly.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded `index.html`, `css/style.css`, and all JS modules: `utils.js`, `audio.js`, `input.js`, `particles.js`, `stickman.js`, `fighters.js`, `world.js`, `ui.js`, `game.js`, `main.js`.
- Implemented player combat, enemy AI types (grunt/ninja/brute/boss), waves, boss bar, combos/score/best score, pickups, pause/gameover/victory overlays, touch joystick/buttons, mute, gamepad polling, debug hook `window.__stickSmash`.
- Started dev server with `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"` inside tmux session `game`; `curl localhost:3002` returns 200.
- Installed missing Playwright Chromium via `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`; opened title screen in session `dev`.
- Captured `screenshots/title.png` and `screenshots/game1.png`; verified page runs, gameplay reaches wave 1 with 3 enemies, and visuals broadly work.
- Identified and partially fixed issues: missing `updateCamera` declaration, duplicate `ui.updateHud` call in render, menu duplicate pose update, removal of overlapping initial/boss callouts, victory timeout run-ID guard, stray `irc:` label, wave total/start best fields.
- Rewrote `js/world.js` with baked sky/ground/sign sprites, batched rain, cached props, softer reflections, reduced window density, and dynamic barrels/steam overlays.

### Active
- Browser-run verification after the world.js rewrite; need to reload and re-screenshot gameplay/title, check console errors.
- Performance is very poor under SwiftShader (~5 fps at 1050×793, dpr 1); render command timings were only ~18 ms per frame, indicating raster/fill-rate bottleneck. Need to measure post-bake FPS and decide on adaptive internal render scale.
- Gameplay spacing issue observed: all enemies converge and overlap around player; planned fixes not yet applied (preferred side + depth offset per enemy, stronger separation, player foot ring/marker).
- Visual polish pending: scale/baseline adjustment (suggested `s = min(W/1080, H/740)`, desktop baseline ~0.66), less repetitive/brighter city, rage label duplication (`FURIA` shown twice; right hint should read `ESPECIAL · L`), maybe larger characters.

### Blocked
- None functional; performance tuning is the main risk.

## Next Move
1. Reload `http://localhost:3002` in `playwright-cli -s=dev` and verify no JS errors after world.js rewrite; capture title + gameplay screenshots.
2. Add enemy positioning: per-enemy `sideBias` and `yOffset` so they surround the player instead of stacking; strengthen `Game.separate()` depth push; spawn y near player ± offset.
3. Fix HUD rage hint text and adjust camera scale/baseline for stronger character presence.
4. Measure FPS; if still low under SwiftShader add adaptive internal render resolution (e.g. 0.65–0.8 backing store scaled by CSS) or further background optimizations.
5. Test combat inputs (punch combo, kick, jump, block, dodge, special), waves, boss, game over/victory, pause, mute, and mobile 390×844 touch layout with screenshots.
6. Run final capture via `capture.sh`/Playwright and confirm the start button auto-click path works.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM structure, HUD, overlays, touch controls, start button.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: full neon UI styling and responsive layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: game loop/state, waves, combat resolution, camera, render pipeline.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/fighters.js`: Fighter class, player controls, enemy AI, attack definitions, waves.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: baked background/sky/ground rendering, rain, props, signs (just rewritten).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/stickman.js`: procedural skeleton poses/drawing and ground shadows.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/ui.js`: DOM HUD/banner/overlay/touch bindings.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: keyboard/virtual joystick/gamepad input.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/particles.js`: sparks, dust, rings, floating text.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: WebAudio SFX + procedural music.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: bootstrap, frame loop, debug surface.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/title.png`, `screenshots/game1.png`: latest visual evidence.

## Important Context
- Dev server runs in tmux session `game`; logs at `/tmp/opencode/server.log`; port 3002.
- Playwright CLI session `dev` is open at `http://localhost:3002`.
- `window.__stickSmash` exposes `{ start, pause, resume, state, snapshot }`; `snapshot()` reports state/wave/enemies/hp/fps.
- Clicking by text `JUGAR` failed in playwright-cli; use `window.__stickSmash.start()` or the `Play game` accessible label.
- Capture harness auto-click regex matches accessible button labels `Start`, `Play`, `Start game`, `Play game`, etc.; Spanish button text alone will not auto-trigger.
- Under SwiftShader FPS is ~5; snapshot FPS can be misleading immediately after `eval` because `last` frame timestamp is involved.
- Enemy spawn queue/order was randomized in `startWave`, and boss spawns first followed by ninjas.
- No commits made; all project files are currently untracked/new in git (branch `opencode/41229979976`).
- Current work is uncommitted/unpushed.

## Objective
- Build a polished stickman beat 'em up ("smash 'em up") browser game in Spanish, playable on desktop and mobile, with combos, enemies, and a final boss.

## Requirements
- Stickman fighters with beat 'em up combat (combos, enemy waves, boss).
- Browser-playable with no external assets/frameworks; static project served on port 3002.
- Responsive desktop and touch controls (repo mobile-game conventions).
- Verify in a real browser with screenshots, not just unit tests.
- Start button must remain auto-clickable by the capture harness (`aria-label="Play game"`).

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS ES modules + Canvas 2D; no package.json/Vite; Spanish UI.
- Neon-noir rainy city street/rooftop theme; procedural stick figures and WebAudio-synthesized SFX/music.
- Five waves ending with boss "EL REY"; continuous scrolling stage.
- Controls: WASD/arrows move, J/Z punch (3-hit combo), K/X kick, Space jump, Shift/B block, Q/Ctrl dodge, L/C special (50 fury), Esc/P pause, M mute, Enter start.
- Background layers baked to offscreen canvases; title screen uses a lightweight non-baked floor.
- Menu/canvas renders at 0.5 backing scale to keep the title responsive under SwiftShader.
- Title screen canvas is static (rendered once per state); CSS animations still animate the DOM.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded `index.html`, `css/style.css`, all JS modules; game runs on port 3002.
- Implemented player combat, four enemy types, waves, boss bar, combos/score/best score, pickups, pause/gameover/victory overlays, touch joystick/buttons, mute, gamepad, debug hook `window.__stickSmash`.
- Fixed missing `updateCamera`, duplicate `ui.updateHud`, duplicate menu pose update, victory timeout run-ID guard, stray `irc:` label, wave fields.
- Rewrote `js/world.js` with baked sky/ground/signs, batched rain, softer reflections; fixed missing `hexA()` helper.
- Enemy formation: per-enemy `sideBias`, `slotOffset`, `depthBias`, lane collapse when allies die; alternating spawn sides; stronger separation; opening crew pre-spawned around player.
- Player foot ring added; scale enlarged (`s = min(W/1120, H/720)`, desktop baseline 0.71); HUD rage hint changed to `ESPECIAL · L`.
- Fixed `setPointerCapture` synthetic-pointer crash in `js/input.js`.
- Added visible joystick/block/punch touch testing; keyboard Enter/J/Escape path verified.
- Verified combat, special attack, boss wave, wave progression, victory, game over, pause, desktop and mobile layouts with screenshots.
- Capture flow: desktop/mobile auto-start now clicks successfully in some runs; intermittent `locator.click: Timeout 2000ms` still occurs during the first few seconds.

### Active
- Hunting the intermittent start-button click timeout in `capture.sh`/`default-capture.mjs` (harness trial/actual click waits "visible, enabled and stable"). Latest hypothesis: initial full-page paint blocks rAF ~3 seconds around 0.8–4s; button geometry itself stays fixed.
- Test file `/tmp/opencode/debug-static.mjs` was just written to compare control vs fully static CSS; not yet run.

### Blocked
- None functional; click-timeout reliability under SwiftShader is the main remaining risk.

## Next Move
1. Run `node /tmp/opencode/debug-static.mjs` to compare click timings with all CSS animations/filters disabled.
2. If CSS paint is the cause, permanently remove/lighten expensive title effects (`backdrop-filter`, large logo filters, `screen-fx` scanlines) and re-test capture 5×.
3. If rAF is blocked by the canvas paint, defer or pre-warm the first menu render; ensure start button is clickable before the first heavy composite.
4. Re-run `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=... ./capture.sh` several times until desktop and mobile auto-start are reliable.
5. Clear `localStorage` best score before final screenshots; capture final title, gameplay, boss, victory and mobile shots.
6. Optionally add game-specific README section; verify no console errors and commit changes (currently all files untracked, no commits).

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: frame loop, menu/static one-shot rendering, debug hook.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: state, waves, opening crew, camera, render, separation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/fighters.js`: combat, player input, enemy slot AI, waves/types.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: baked sky/ground/signs, menu-mode ground, rain, props.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: title animations, start button, overlays, responsive/touch styles.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: HUD, overlays, `#startBtn` with `aria-label="Play game"`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/ui.js`: HUD/overlays/touch bindings, rage hint.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: keyboard, virtual/touch joystick, gamepad.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/stickman.js`: pose generation and drawing.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/particles.js`: sparks, rings, floating text.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: WebAudio SFX/music.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: capture entry point (`CAPTURE_URL`, `CAPTURE_DIR` required).
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/capture-start.mjs`: auto-start logic causing intermittent timeout.
- `/tmp/opencode/debug-static.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/debug-nuke.mjs`, `/tmp/opencode/debug-rect.mjs`: click-timing diagnostics.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest visual evidence (`game4.png`, `boss.png`, `victory.png`, `game-mobile.png`, etc.).

Still failures, and now aria never clears (markers []), and there's a ~1.7s gap between scans (e.g., 837→2624). Why? The menu render at 1400ms stalls for ~1.7s. But the button should have become ready before 1400ms — readiness requires 4 smooth frames. Why didn't it? Perhaps even a blank canvas + title overlay page has slow frames in fresh Chromium until the menu render? No, readiness markers [] means `aria-disabled` never removed even after 3.7s. Wait, markers observe only if MutationObserver attached at DOMContentLoaded and button exists; markers [] could also mean the observer didn't attach (script order). In run 0 earlier (before our changes) markers [] once too. Let's verify readiness directly in this environment.

The scans show 0 matches because aria-disabled is 'true' (or buttons hidden). Readiness not achieved. Maybe smoothFrames threshold <140ms is too strict: in this environment frames are ~150-250ms even when "blank". Earlier ready test showed ready between 1.7-2.7s, so it did happen. But now with menu delayed/hidden, why not?

Wait: `ui.markReady()` sets `this.ready`; `ui` is defined. But is `smoothFrames` reached? Let's instrument. Also the 1.7s gap suggests the menu render at 1.4s still happens (because state menu and menuSceneShown false) and blocks. But readiness should be true by then. Unless frames are consistently >140ms due to the title overlay text effects/compositing. Let me directly measure aria/ready with timestamps again (debug-ready) after changes.
